observations: GNUNET_DHT_get_start accepts the lookup key as const struct GNUNET_HashCode *key.
GNUNET_HashCode is defined as a 512-bit hashcode and GNUNET_CRYPTO_HASH_LENGTH is 512/8 bytes.

A Git SHA-1 object id is 160 bits. Therefore a raw 20-byte Git SHA-1 cannot be the complete native GNUNET_HashCode value without an embedding, padding, hashing, KDF, namespace mapping, or other deterministic transformation into 512 bits.

GNUnet GET can return bytes to the caller, so returned candidate bytes could in principle still be locally checked against Git canonical object hashing; this does not repair the exact-key identity mismatch.
No passive lookup was issued and no independently pre-existing residency of the target Git object in GNUnet was established.
probe.inference: GNUnet DHT fails this candidate's exact-key identity criterion at the API representation layer: its native lookup key is 512 bits, so preserving an exact 160-bit Git SHA-1 as the complete caller-visible DHT key requires an additional transformation or mapping convention. Local Git verification remains possible for returned bytes, but both exact native key binding and pre-existing residency are required by this Phase-1 leaf, so acceptance remains fail-closed.
probe.tested_scope: GNUnet public primary API/header/tutorial semantics for DHT GET key type and GNUNET_HashCode width; source-level audit only. No network GET, PUT, publication, hosted query/project, mapping service, or target-residency test.

assumptions_uncertainty_residuals.assumption: The leaf requires the native caller-visible DHT key itself to preserve the exact Git SHA-1 identity, not merely a reversible embedding convention.
assumptions_uncertainty_residuals.uncertainty: A specific application may define a deterministic 160-to-512-bit embedding, but that is precisely an added transformation/mapping layer and was not accepted by the frozen continuation criterion.
assumptions_uncertainty_residuals.residual: Returned bytes remain locally Git-verifiable in principle, but passive pre-existing residency is unproven and the native key-identity requirement already fails.
